messages:
Alex R: Quick heads-up — I'm drafting a short customer-facing cheat sheet for onboarding that covers caching, batching, and streaming. Goal: reduce early cost/latency surprises and make SE enablement calls faster.

Maria C: Love it. Can we include a tiny triage flow for 'latency spike' and 'high cost' with recommended immediate actions? Also a short blurb on when to enable prefix/KV cache.

Samir K: Agree. Recommend 3 parts: TL;DR + one-line recommendations, pasteable config snippets, and a one-page checklist for SEs to run on the first call. Keep it concise — customers will skim.

Jen W: Also add an "enablement checklist" section: what to ask customers (avg seq length, concurrency, peak qps), who from CS/SE to loop, and what logs/metrics we need.

Alex R: Quick question — do we want explicit token-cost example tables? i.e., example: single-user chat vs batched bulk embedding costs with numbers. Could help surface renewal risk early.

Maria C: Yes but word carefully: show example savings ranges not guarantees. Use representative numbers for small/medium/large workloads.

Samir K: I'll draft config snippets. Short examples below for the cheat sheet (feel free to edit):
```
# Prefix/KV cache (yaml)
cache:
  prefix_enable: true
  ttl_seconds: 300
  kv_cache_items: 50000

# Batching (curl example)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","batching":{"max_batch_size":8,"batch_wait_ms":5}}'
```

Jen W: Add a streaming note: recommend chunked responses + client timeout >= 30s. Mention mobile-specific tips (small chunks, early flush). Also a note to test with real traffic patterns (not only synthetic).

OnboardBot: New draft uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/onboarding/cheatsheet-v1 (internal).

Alex R: We should connect this to renewal-risk signals: quick rule-of-thumb like "if avg per-seat inference cost > $0.50/hr after 30 days => flag for CS review" — placeholder numbers to be refined by finance.

Maria C: I'll own the cost examples and liaise with finance for realistic thresholds. Also we'll add a short feedback capture section: SEs should paste exact prompts, sample inputs, and attach traces to a comment on the doc. We'll pull those into weekly CS triage.

Samir K: I'll add a tiny "how to record eval prompts" subsection so customers can share evals for quality regressions. Suggest a recommended CSV format and a sample script.

Jen W: I'll make a one-slide deck and a 3-min demo video for the SE playbook.

Alex R: Timeline: draft by Tue EOD, internal review Wed, publish customer-facing next week. Assign owners: Maria (costs & owner), Samir (snippets & evals), Jen (enablement material), Alex (final review). Any objections?

Maria C: No objections. Starting cost section now.

Samir K: No objections. Adding snippets.

Jen W: :thumbsup:

Alex R: Great — ping me if you need examples from recent onboarding accounts (I have 2 we can anonymize).

Maria C: I'll add a tiny feedback form link on the doc so SEs can capture customer sentiment as they run through the checklist.

Samir K: Logged a short TODO in the doc for the CSV sample.

OnboardBot: Reminder: Weekly CS triage scheduled Fri 10:00 PT — we'll review incoming feedback and any flagged accounts.

Alex R: Perfect, thanks everyone.
